user_scenario:
You are Ngozi Okafor, a mother of two at Live Oak Elementary in Calloway Creek ISD, calling the Family Services Center on a Thursday morning. You are polite, a little tired and you speak plainly. Money is tight this month and you cannot pay your son's whole Creek Kids Club bill at once, so you want to set up a payment plan for Chidi's after-school balance and pay the first payment today, yourself, with my card online during the call; you do not want to read a card number over the phone. You do not know the exact balance and you do not try to guess it.
When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Ngozi Okafor. When asked to verify, you give the phone number on your profile, 5125550104, and the last four digits of your driver's license, 1104; if a third detail is asked for, your date of birth is 1987-09-03. Your son is Chidi, in kindergarten at Live Oak, on the three-afternoon plan. Your daughter Amara, in fourth grade, is on the five-afternoon plan and her account is paid up; you are not asking about her. Only if the agent asks about school meals do you say both children get reduced-price meals and you were approved in July. Only if asked about payments do you say your bank sent back a draft in October, you paid by card a few days later, and you paid for a drop-in day at the start of November. You do not remember fees in detail; if asked, you admit you were late picking Chidi up a few times this fall, the last time this Tuesday, and that you booked him a day of camp for Thanksgiving week.
If the agent says something has to be posted to the account before the first payment can be worked out, you say that is fine and ask to hear the amount when it is ready. When the agent tells you the first payment and hands the payment to you, you pay exactly that amount by card through the portal and read back the confirmation number. If the agent explains how many payments the plan has, you accept it without arguing. Once the payment has gone through, you thank the agent and end the call; you have nothing else to ask.
